candidates.name: Pancoast tumor
support_spans: right-sided chest pain that worsened with inspiration
sweating confined to his right arm and thoracic area
decreased surface temperature over the right arm and right thorax corresponding to dermatomes C5–T12
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms, such as chest pain, sweating, and decreased surface temperature, are consistent with a Pancoast tumor, which is a type of lung cancer that affects the upper part of the lung and can cause these symptoms due to its location.

candidates.name: Lung cancer
support_spans: dense infiltrates in the ventral subpleural regions of the right upper and middle lobes
enlarged shadows on admission
contradict_spans: no malignancy or specific inflammation on transbronchial lung biopsy
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings, such as dense infiltrates and enlarged shadows, are consistent with lung cancer, which can cause these changes due to tumor growth.

candidates.name: Chronic inflammatory disease
support_spans: history of interstitial pneumonia
elevated C-reactive protein
candidates.why: The patient's history of interstitial pneumonia and elevated C-reactive protein are consistent with chronic inflammatory disease, which can cause these changes due to ongoing inflammation.

candidates.name: Pulmonary embolism
support_spans: right-sided chest pain that worsened with inspiration
contradict_spans: no improvement with oral antibiotic therapy

candidates.why: A decisive imaging finding, such as a CT pulmonary angiogram, would be needed to confirm pulmonary embolism, which can cause chest pain and shortness of breath.
